reason: Intro page states the application layer, seventh OSI layer, and rule evaluation in priority order leading to a target from the rule action's target group.
The stickiness.lb_cookie.duration_seconds attribute (duration-based cookie) has min 1 second, max 7 days (604800 s), default 1 day (86400 s).
LCU Details lists 1 GB per hour for EC2, containers and IP targets and 0.4 GB per hour for Lambda targets.
Pricing page: each LCU provides 1,000 rule evaluations per second (averaged over the hour); FAQ repeats it for Lambda targets.
The 25 per second figure is stated, but Note 1 on the same list limits it for HTTPS listeners to RSA keys of 2K or less and ECDSA keys of 256 or less; the claim drops this condition.
LCU Details: 3,000 active connections per minute, or 1,500 while using Mutual TLS.
Rule evaluations definition says the first 10 processed rules are free; Note 2 says with 10 or fewer rules configured the dimension is ignored.
Capacity reservation page: the total reservation request must be at least 100 LCU.
Routes to targets with the lowest number of in-progress requests; commonly used when requests or targets vary.
FAQ answer to which TCP ports can be used to load balance on an ALB: 1-65535 (listener page also lists ports 1-65535).
Listener configuration: listeners support Protocols HTTP, HTTPS.

Metrics table row: number of HTTP 5XX server error codes that originate from the load balancer, not including target responses.
Metrics table row: time elapsed, in seconds, after the request leaves the load balancer until the target starts to send response headers.
Metrics table row: UnHealthyHostCount is the number of targets that are considered unhealthy.

The two quoted options match the claim: passthrough sends the entire chain without verifying; verify performs X.509 client certificate authentication during TLS negotiation.
The three-step list matches: create trust store, upload CA bundle and optionally revocation lists, attach to the listener.

Request tracing page: load balancer adds or updates X-Amzn-Trace-Id before sending to the target; used to track HTTP requests from clients to targets.
Round robin routes evenly across healthy targets in sequential order; commonly used for similar requests and similar targets.
Quote: round robin by default, LOR and weighted random also available, only one active algorithm per target group at a time.
Quote: each rule must include exactly one of forward, redirect or fixed-response, and it must be the last action performed.
Access log field: a matched rule's priority is a value from 1 to 50,000; 0 when no rule matched and the default action was taken.
Quote states rules are evaluated from lowest to highest priority value and the default rule is evaluated last.
User guide steps for Application Load Balancers: evaluate rules in priority order, then select a target using the target group's algorithm; default is round robin.
Quote states the ALB security group controls the traffic allowed to reach and leave the load balancer.
Quote defines a security policy as an SSL negotiation configuration, a combination of protocols and ciphers, used to negotiate SSL connections between client and load balancer.
Quote: security group rules must allow traffic in both directions on both the listener and health check ports.
slow_start.duration_seconds: range 30-900 seconds (15 minutes), default 0 seconds (disabled).
Certificate list supports multiple domains on one port with a different certificate each; the smart selection algorithm uses SNI and the client-provided hostname.
Quote: with sticky sessions the algorithm is used for initial selection; later requests from the same client go to the same target, bypassing it.
Both cookie types supported, enabled at target group level; application-based when the app has its own session cookie, duration-based when it does not.
Quotes: useful for servers that maintain state information; the client must support cookies.
Considerations: sticky sessions are not supported when cross-zone is disabled (attempts fail); application-based stickiness does not work with weighted target groups.
Quote: session affinity binds a user's session to a specific target, all requests in the session go to it, and the client must support cookies.
Quote: each Availability Zone subnet needs a CIDR with at least a /27 bitmask and at least eight free IP addresses so the load balancer can scale.
Quotes: select at least two Availability Zone subnets; each subnet must be from a different Availability Zone.
Troubleshooting HTTP 504 cause: failed to establish a connection to the target before the connection timeout expired (10 seconds).
Quotes: each target group can be used with only one load balancer; a target can be registered with multiple target groups.
Quote: by default weighted target groups do not guarantee sticky sessions; enable target group stickiness on the rule; cookie named AWSALBTG encodes the selected target group.
Quote: TLS connections to targets use installed certificates, are not validated, so self-signed or expired certificates can be used.
Three quotes: sticky sessions not supported with target optimizer, routing can only be round robin, traffic incurs more LCU usage than regular target groups.
Quote: by default routes using the target group's protocol and port; the port can be overridden per target at registration.
Target health table: draining means the target is deregistering and connection draining is in process.
Target health table: initial means registering the target or performing the initial health checks.
Target health table: unhealthy means the target did not respond to a health check or failed it.
